cards.q: What is a black hole in terms of matter?
cards.a: A huge concentration of matter packed into a very tiny space.

cards.q: What are accretion disks around black holes?
cards.a: Rings of gas and dust that emit light across many wavelengths, including X-rays.

cards.q: What is the supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way called?

cards.a: Ripples in the fabric of space-time created when very massive objects accelerate through space.
The bending and distortion of light from more distant objects by massive objects like black holes.

cards.q: Why can nothing escape from just beneath a black hole's event horizon?
cards.a: Gravity there is strong enough that nothing, not even light, can escape.

cards.q: Why are black holes effectively invisible to telescopes?
cards.a: They don't emit or reflect light.

cards.q: Why does the accretion disk appear to wrap above and below the black hole in NASA's artist's concept?
cards.a: The black hole's gravity bends light from the far side of the disk.

cards.q: How did astronomers prove the Milky Way's center houses a supermassive black hole?
cards.a: By tracking the orbits of several stars near the center.

cards.q: What can gravitational lensing be used to find?
cards.a: Isolated black holes that are otherwise invisible.

cards.q: Which telescope detected bright flares and fainter flickers from Sagittarius A*?

Is a black hole's event horizon a surface like Earth's or the Sun's?
cards.a: No; it is a boundary that contains all the matter that makes up the black hole.
No; they don't provide shortcuts between different points in space, or portals to other dimensions or universes.
